notes: Identity independently checked from supplied text: printed title Can Physical Warmth (or Coldness) Predict Trait Loneliness? A Replication of Bargh and Shalev (2012), authors Jessica Wortman, M. Brent Donnellan, and Richard E. Lucas, Archives of Scientific Psychology 2014, 2, 13–19, and DOI 10.1037/arc0000007 match the neutral replication reference (canonical L20–31). This is a StudyLib-hosted transcription of the primary empirical article, not an original Study 2 source or a preregistration. The cached artifact contains overlapping line-numbered web-render sections and a truncation marker; the identity, full Critical Analyses paragraph, supplemental analyses, and discussion are visible. No supplied PDF exists, so no PDF rendering was possible. Primary target identified by the replication of original Study 2, loneliness outcome, warm/cold experimental comparison, and article p. 4 locator, independently of numeric values or row position. Retained printed d=.02 and p=.995 for the same primary test despite the very small printed t; no recomputation or metric conversion. The effect is explicitly scored with positive scores indicating greater loneliness in the cold group (L382–384). Supplemental analyses on the same page include correlations, a controlled regression, semester subsets, manipulation-check exclusions, and belief/suspicion subsets; those are explicitly supplemental rather than alternative primary target tests. Original and replication n are unassigned placeholders and must not overwrite previously verified fields. No analytic N was derived.
